R0161.title: Cross-Chain Bridge Attacks
R0161.definition: Attacks targeting blockchain cross-chain bridge protocols by exploiting bridge contract vulnerabilities or validation mechanism flaws to steal locked assets.
R0161.description: Cross-chain bridges facilitate asset transfers between different blockchains, typically requiring assets to be locked on the source chain and equivalent tokens minted on the target chain. Attackers can exploit bridge contract vulnerabilities, multi-signature validation flaws, or oracle manipulation to mint tokens without locking assets, or directly steal assets from the locked pool.
R0161.influence: Causes cross-chain bridge fund pool theft, user cross-chain asset losses, and impacts multi-chain ecosystem interoperability.

observables: The cross-chain bridge contract mints target-chain tokens without locking sufficient assets
Bridge multi-signature validation shows transaction records with anomalous signatures or bypassed validation thresholds
Locked pool assets are transferred in large amounts to unfamiliar addresses within a short window, accompanied by anomalous cross-chain messages
The cross-chain message validation logic is triggered on an abnormal branch, with a signer set inconsistent with the preset
